summary.whatChanges: The prettyJSON middleware now detects JSON responses with a regex instead of a `startsWith('application/json')` check. Structured-suffix types like `application/problem+json` and `application/vnd.api+json` are now pretty-printed, while lookalikes such as `application/json-seq` are left untouched. Tests cover both cases.
behaviorChanges: Responses with `+json` content types (e.g. application/problem+json, application/vnd.api+json) are now re-serialized with indentation when pretty printing is active.
Responses with content types that merely start with `application/json`, such as `application/json-seq`, are no longer parsed or reformatted and pass through unchanged.
Content-Type matching is now case-insensitive and tolerates parameters/whitespace after the type (e.g. `; charset=utf-8`).
risks: Any caller that relied on streaming/sequence JSON types being reformatted will see raw output instead.

Pretty-printing `+json` bodies buffers and re-parses the whole response, so previously untouched large or streamed vendor-JSON responses are now fully read into memory and will error if the body is not valid JSON.
The regex only accepts `application/...`; JSON-ish types under other top-level types (e.g. text/json) remain unhandled.
